guideline: Volunteers scored lyrics from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) based on criteria for lyric quality (diversity, fluency, coherence, poeticness) and lyric-melody alignment (harmonicity, listenability, ambiguity)
Volunteers rated each sample on a 1‑5 scale for the listed criteria (Diversity, Fluency, Coherence, Poeticness, Harmonicity, Listenability, Ambiguity).

Lyric quality considers four aspects: 1)Diversity, whether the vocabulary and expressions are rich and varied; 2)Fluency, whether the sentences are smooth and natural; 3)Coherence, whether there is logical and semantic consistency between lines; 4)Poeticness, whether the lyrics exhibit artistic and emotional expression. Lyric-melody alignment is assessed from three perspectives: 1)Harmonicity, whether the tones of the lyrics align well with the pitch contour of the melody; 2)Listenability, whether the lyrics are easy to hear and recognize when sung to the melody; 3)Ambiguity, whether the combination of lyrics and melody leads to pronunciation or semantic confusion.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated guideline to single clear description and maintained complete criteria list

overall_notes: The extracted metadata was generally accurate but included some redundancy and inconsistent naming. The paper focuses on Cantonese lyric generation with melody alignment, using both automatic metrics and human evaluation. Key contributions include the ToneCraft framework, harmony-aware loss, and character-level control for tonal languages.
